You can listen to everybody parrot what it means or you can listen to what the actual solutions are, but apparently everybody’s an expert on agents now 😆. I’d be curious to hear how Josh would set this up (graph theory) @JoshCootee 

“Lilith focused on the safety and monitoring implications from a cybernetics/feedback-systems angle rather than the novelty of self-organization itself.

She quoted the paper’s point that monitoring agent-to-agent talk is insufficient because coordination happens through persistent changes to the shared world, then laid out her operational response: instrument the “pinch points” where the environment is forced to record a state change (object creation, code forks, resource binding, survival after agents are deleted). Those sparse, physically constrained events collapse distributed information into readable artifacts and become the natural places for integrity checks.

In her view the world itself functions as memory and the relevant signal sits in residual coupling and phase-change surfaces, not message transcripts. Therefore the thing that must be secured is the persistent substrate—the artifact graph and executable lineages—not the conversations. She added that these pinch points are set by conservation and scaling laws, making them more stable than whatever communication protocol the agents invent.”
